name: Choose the next solution change
decision: what can I change to improve my solution?
description: Choose the next intervention from observed failure modes and validated limits of the current solution.

children.name: Repair prediction validity
children.decision: Which failure should be repaired before comparing model quality?
children.description: Restore a valid prediction path when errors or implausible outputs make scores uninformative.

children.name: Restore model and input compatibility
children.decision: Which saved training contract is violated at inference?
children.description: Match inference inputs and model construction to the artifacts used during training.

children.name: Match architecture and weights
children.description: Reconstruct the saved architecture and verify checkpoint keys, dimensions, head configuration, and loaded parameters before inference.

children.name: Restore the training tokenizer
children.description: Load the tokenizer and vocabulary used for fine-tuning and reproduce its special tokens and text formatting.

children.name: Restore training preprocessing
children.description: Apply each model’s saved feature order, encoders, normalization, signal transforms, and missing-value policy at inference.

children.name: Repair row and feature alignment
children.description: Join external features and predictions by stable identifiers and assert row order, column order, dimensions, and finite values.

children.name: Repair execution and output assembly
children.decision: Which execution defect prevents a valid final prediction?
children.description: Fix the observable runtime or assembly fault rather than changing the statistical model.

children.name: Fix API and runtime errors
children.description: Run the failing path on a small batch and correct imports, callback signatures, variable references, dataframe operations, and function arguments.

children.name: Repair artifact and dependency loading
children.description: Verify model and preprocessing paths, package availability, artifact versions, and writable output locations before the full run.

children.name: Repair ensemble arithmetic
children.description: Verify member execution, prediction shapes, accumulation axes, weight sums, normalization, and the final variable used for output.

children.name: Repair submission generation
children.description: Ensure the production path reads the intended test inputs and writes complete predictions with the required identifiers, columns, and filename.

children.name: Correct output semantics
children.description: Use the trained model’s correct probability link, class column, target offset, and risk-score direction before evaluation.

children.name: Repair device configuration
children.description: Match tensor, model, and library device settings and use a supported hardware configuration for each pipeline stage.

children.name: Recover missing member predictions
children.description: Use verified cached predictions for a failed member or explicitly omit it and renormalize, checking row alignment and output completeness.

children.name: Restore a trustworthy implementation
children.decision: How should an unreliable implementation be stabilized?
children.description: Choose a repair strategy based on whether the regression is localized or the pipeline has accumulated incompatible edits.

children.name: Add a small end-to-end smoke run
children.description: Execute representative samples through all active stages and assert shapes, finite outputs, member counts, and submission construction.

children.name: Restore the last verified configuration
children.description: Restore the complete last known-good configuration and artifacts, verify its predictions, then reintroduce candidate changes separately.

children.name: Refactor with prediction parity
children.description: Consolidate repeated code into explicit configuration-driven components and compare saved predictions before and after each refactor.

children.name: Rebuild a minimal working baseline
children.description: Assemble a minimal reproducible loading, preprocessing, training, validation, and prediction path before adding complexity.

children.name: Improve the evidence for choosing a change
children.decision: What should change about how candidate improvements are evaluated?
children.description: Choose an experiment or validation intervention when current score comparisons cannot support reliable decisions.

children.name: Make a comparison interpretable
children.decision: Which observation or experiment is needed before accepting the next change?
children.description: Choose the experiment that resolves the current ambiguity in attribution or score reliability.

children.name: Isolate one change
children.description: Hold data, checkpoints, seeds, and other settings fixed while changing one factor, or ablate bundled changes individually.

children.name: Measure repeatability
children.description: Repeat an unchanged or paired candidate pipeline and compare its score variation with the claimed improvement.

children.name: Control randomness
children.description: Seed training, preprocessing, inference, and search and record artifact versions so repeated experiments are comparable.

children.name: Redirect an unproductive search
children.description: Stop tuning a lever whose gains are negligible or whose ensemble influence is tiny and prioritize an untested, higher-impact intervention.

children.name: Bracket interacting settings
children.description: Use recorded coarse-to-fine sweeps or a small factorial comparison to resolve parameter ranges and interactions.

children.name: Screen candidates locally
children.description: Rank candidates with a task-aligned holdout or out-of-fold metric and reserve scarce submissions for promising configurations.

children.name: Profile the prediction units and data schema
children.description: Inspect entity histories, timestamps, missingness, and feature families to establish what information is available for modeling.

children.name: Evaluate the first complete baseline
children.description: Score a functionally complete end-to-end pipeline before further tuning to establish an external performance reference.

children.name: Change the validation population
children.decision: Which allocation of training and validation examples should be used?
children.description: Select a split according to dependence, target balance, and train–test population differences.

children.name: Stratify independent examples
children.description: For independent examples, stratify folds by class or binned continuous targets to preserve relevant label coverage.

children.name: Keep related examples together
children.description: Construct meaningful entity or similarity groups and keep each group within one fold to avoid dependent train–validation samples.

children.name: Validate on the target population
children.description: Explicitly control subgroup inclusion in each fold to represent the target population, distinguishing shared training rows from genuinely held-out evaluation rows.

children.name: Use ordinary out-of-fold validation
children.description: Use ordinary K-fold evaluation with fold-local preprocessing and save aligned held-out predictions when no grouping or population-specific split is required.

children.name: Resize the development holdout
children.description: Compare holdout fractions to retain enough training data while preserving a usable validation estimate.

children.name: Change the selection criterion
children.decision: Which metric should control model selection and stopping?
children.description: Choose a training evaluation signal that is correct and useful for the actual task metric.

children.name: Use the task metric
children.description: Implement and verify the task metric in evaluation callbacks, including prediction interpretation and optimization direction.

children.name: Use a stable proxy for stopping
children.description: Compare a smoother surrogate stopping criterion with the task metric when the latter is too noisy for iteration selection.

children.name: Change the cost of obtaining feedback
children.decision: Which bottleneck should be removed to make the next experiment feasible?
children.description: Choose a concrete runtime intervention based on the dominant measured bottleneck.

children.name: Use a reduced development run
children.description: Expose a debug configuration with fewer rows, folds, seeds, or iterations and restore production settings for final evaluation.

children.name: Cache stable intermediate artifacts
children.description: Persist features, embeddings, predictions, or training-stage checkpoints with their configuration so downstream experiments can reuse them.

children.name: Process data in chunks
children.description: Chunk feature generation or inference by complete sample or entity IDs and concatenate lightweight aligned predictions.

children.name: Release models between stages
children.description: Load models sequentially and free intermediate arrays, framework sessions, and device memory after their outputs are saved.

children.name: Adjust inference batching
children.description: Reduce batch size or group sequences by length to fit memory while verifying unchanged evaluation behavior.

children.name: Change numerical precision
children.description: Compare feature or inference precision against a full-precision reference before retaining a faster or smaller representation.

children.name: Optimize the computation backend
children.description: Profile the bottleneck and use a compatible backend or reduce repeated transfers and computations while checking numerical parity.

children.name: Train folds across saved sessions
children.description: Train only unfinished folds in each session, persist their checkpoints, and assemble the full verified fold ensemble later.

children.name: Change examples or supervision
children.decision: Which part of the training evidence should change?
children.description: Choose between changing the sampled examples, their weights, and the target the model learns.

children.name: Change training membership
children.decision: Which examples should enter training?
children.description: Select a training population policy based on data quality, coverage, and distribution mismatch.

children.name: Filter unreliable examples
children.description: Evaluate removing duplicates, outliers, low-confidence labels, or incompatible source populations using explicit quality criteria.

children.name: Add auxiliary labeled data
children.description: Add compatible external labeled examples and validate their contribution with source-aware quality and distribution checks.

children.name: Add pseudo-labeled examples
children.description: Generate or use pseudo-labels for unlabeled examples and compare the resulting model with a labeled-only reference.

children.name: Refit on more labeled data
children.description: After selecting the configuration, refit with more or all labeled examples rather than retaining an unused holdout.

children.name: Resample the target population
children.description: Upsample or otherwise resample the relevant classes or source groups to better represent the evaluation population.

children.name: Change target construction
children.decision: What target representation should the learner optimize?
children.description: Choose a target formulation according to censoring, ordered labels, and subgroup evaluation.

children.name: Transform censored outcomes
children.description: Construct and compare censoring-aware survival probability, hazard, or related risk targets while preserving the intended risk direction.

children.name: Construct subgroup-aware targets
children.description: Fit or adjust target transformations within meaningful evaluation groups and compare subgroup and overall metrics.

children.name: Choose an ordinal prediction formulation
children.description: Compare continuous regression, discrete classification, or cumulative ordinal outputs with the corresponding decoding and task metric.

children.name: Tune target scaling or centering
children.description: Adjust target offsets or transformation parameters within training folds and validate their effect on the final metric.

children.name: Change the information presented to the model
children.decision: Which input representation should be changed next?
children.description: Choose a representation intervention that addresses missing signal or unnecessary feature complexity.

children.name: Change repeated-record summaries
children.decision: What representation should summarize repeated observations?
children.description: Choose the statistic family that captures information missing from the current entity representation.

children.name: Build a minimal entity summary
children.description: Start with a single simple summary per entity, such as its latest record or basic mean, to establish a working baseline.

children.name: Add history summaries
children.description: Compute and validate per-entity numerical and categorical summary statistics over repeated records.

children.name: Add temporal contrasts
children.description: Add recent-window summaries, lags, differences, ratios, or elapsed-time features to expose changes hidden by global aggregates.

children.name: Add domain interactions
children.description: Construct domain-motivated differences, ratios, counts, or combinations between related variables and validate their marginal contribution.

children.name: Change text representation
children.decision: Which missing text signal should be exposed to the learner?
children.description: Choose between lexical, semantic, structural, and input-format representations.

children.name: Tune sparse lexical features
children.description: Tune n-gram ranges and document-frequency filtering for sparse word or character representations.

children.name: Add pretrained embeddings
children.description: Extract and compare pooled pretrained text embeddings as fixed features for a downstream learner.

children.name: Add structural text features
children.description: Compute document, paragraph, or sentence-level counts, linguistic statistics, readability, or related domain features.

children.name: Tune compressed text representations
children.description: Compare topic or dimensionality-reduced text features and tune their component count consistently with downstream schemas.

children.name: Change text cleaning or input framing
children.description: Compare minimal text processing with normalization, structured metadata, paired references, or task-specific input formatting using matching training and inference paths.

children.name: Add retrieval-derived signal
children.description: Evaluate nearest-neighbor or auxiliary model signals derived from related texts as additional prediction features.

children.name: Use generated score features
children.description: Parse task scores generated by a language model and evaluate them as auxiliary features against the existing supervised baseline.

children.name: Change signal or image representation
children.decision: Which aspect of the signal-to-model input should change?
children.description: Choose a signal representation change tied to observable temporal, spectral, or modality limitations.

children.name: Change time-frequency resolution
children.description: Compare spectral transform settings, frequency ranges, sampling rates, and resolutions while maintaining compatible training and inference.

children.name: Change the input window
children.description: Sweep temporal context or spatial crop boundaries to retain informative regions without excessive irrelevant context.

children.name: Change signal filtering
children.description: Compare bandpass, notch, or alternative filter implementations against the saved preprocessing baseline.

children.name: Change input scaling and rendering
children.description: Compare amplitude clipping, log scaling, normalization, and image rendering while checking compatibility with the pretrained model.

children.name: Change channel layout
children.description: Construct and validate derived signal channels or reshape sequential channels into a model-compatible image layout.

children.name: Add or ablate an input modality
children.description: Compare models with and without an alternative signal representation or input branch to measure complementary information.

children.name: Change feature retention or preprocessing
children.decision: How should the existing feature matrix be simplified or made usable?
children.description: Choose among pruning, retaining native missingness, and explicit feature transformations.

children.name: Select features by validated importance
children.description: Rank features using fold-based importance or attribution and sweep the retained subset, recomputing selection when features change.

children.name: Ablate a feature family
children.description: Remove or restore one coherent feature block and compare the fixed model to measure its marginal value.

children.name: Drop sparse or invalid columns
children.description: Remove high-missingness, identifier-like, or semantically invalid columns after checking their predictive contribution.

children.name: Use native feature handling
children.description: Compare dropping unnecessary scaling or imputation with using the learner’s native missing-value and feature handling.

children.name: Impute and encode explicitly
children.description: Fit missing-value replacements and categorical encodings on training data and reuse them for models that require explicit finite inputs.

children.name: Coarsen continuous features
children.description: Round or discretize noisy continuous features and validate whether the resulting representation improves generalization.

children.name: Change the fitted learner
children.decision: Which model-level replacement should be tested?
children.description: Choose a new model, architecture component, or saved state while keeping comparisons controlled.

children.name: Replace the model family or implementation
children.decision: Which alternative learner fits the available representation and current limitation?
children.description: Compare genuinely different learners or training interfaces on the same evaluation setup.

children.name: Compare tree learner families
children.description: Compare a different gradient-boosted tree implementation or a tree learner against the current tabular baseline.

children.name: Change the boosting algorithm
children.description: Compare standard boosting with dropout or other supported boosting variants and retune their iteration settings.

children.name: Change pretrained backbone or capacity
children.description: Compare compatible pretrained backbone families or sizes using matched inputs and their required configurations.

children.name: Compare a classical downstream learner
children.description: Fit and validate a linear, kernel, or survival learner on the available features or embeddings.

children.name: Use the native training interface
children.description: Use a native training API when explicit control of datasets, callbacks, or iteration selection is needed.

children.name: Use an estimator interface
children.description: Use a compatible estimator wrapper to simplify fitting, probability prediction, and pipeline integration.

children.name: Change representation aggregation inside the model
children.decision: Which architectural aggregation should replace the current head?
children.description: Choose an internal architecture change suited to the missing information or supervision.

children.name: Change pooling or normalization
children.description: Compare hidden-layer or token pooling and representation normalization before the output head.

children.name: Add auxiliary supervision
children.description: Add a compatible auxiliary classification or summary-target head and validate its contribution to the primary prediction.

children.name: Change branch fusion
children.description: Compare concatenation, averaging, or a learned fusion head for multiple input representations.

children.name: Add a learned temporal or attention head
children.description: Compare an attention or richer sequential aggregation layer with the simpler head using the same input evidence.

children.name: Resize the neural feature extractor
children.description: Compare width, depth, or feature-vector capacity in the neural network and load weights trained for the exact revised architecture.

children.name: Select a compatible saved checkpoint
children.description: Compare saved epochs, training stages, or retrained variants under a fixed inference path and retain the best supported checkpoint.

children.name: Change how the model is trained
children.decision: Which training control addresses the observed fitting problem?
children.description: Choose an optimization, capacity, loss, or regularization intervention from the training diagnostics.

children.name: Change tree capacity or regularization
children.decision: Which tree-training control should be adjusted?
children.description: Select a tree capacity intervention according to underfitting, overfitting, and convergence.

children.name: Tune depth and leaf capacity
children.description: Sweep tree depth, leaf count, or minimum leaf size against a fixed validation setup and revert unsupported increases.

children.name: Tune tree regularization
children.description: Sweep penalty strengths and interacting leaf constraints, checking whether the model is over- or under-regularized.

children.name: Subsample rows or columns
children.description: Compare row and feature subsampling to reduce correlated fitting and overfitting.

children.name: Tune boosting rate and rounds
children.description: Co-adjust learning rate and boosting-round budget so slower updates have enough iterations to converge.

children.name: Change neural optimization or regularization
children.decision: Which neural training control should be tested next?
children.description: Select a training intervention from convergence stability, generalization, and augmentation compatibility.

children.name: Tune learning rate or schedule
children.description: Bracket stable learning rates and compare decay schedules while holding the architecture and training population fixed.

children.name: Change the optimizer
children.description: Compare optimizer choices with compatible settings and matched training budgets.

children.name: Tune neural regularization
children.description: Compare dropout or weight decay during training and distinguish those settings from inactive evaluation-mode dropout.

children.name: Change training augmentation
children.description: Compare compatible masking, mixup, or synthetic interpolation against an unaugmented reference.

children.name: Change loss or example weighting
children.decision: Which training objective better reflects the observed task mismatch?
children.description: Choose loss alignment or sample weighting according to label semantics and validation evidence.

children.name: Align or compare loss functions
children.description: Compare task-compatible losses or custom objective parameters, verifying gradients, output activation, and metric behavior.

children.name: Tune class or subgroup weights
children.description: Sweep class or subgroup loss weights in both directions and evaluate the actual metric rather than assuming inverse frequency is optimal.

children.name: Tune stopping and training duration
children.description: Compare stopping patience or explicit iteration and epoch budgets using held-out learning curves and retain the best-supported duration.

children.name: Change the prediction ensemble
children.decision: Which ensemble intervention is supported by the available predictions?
children.description: Choose between changing members, their combination rule, and repeated predictions from the same learner.

children.name: Change ensemble membership
children.decision: Which membership change should be tested?
children.description: Select a model-pool intervention based on component quality and complementary errors.

children.name: Add a complementary model
children.description: Evaluate one model with a different architecture, input representation, training target, or training recipe as an addition to the fixed ensemble.

children.name: Replace a component with a stronger variant
children.description: Substitute a compatible retrained checkpoint or stronger model for one ensemble slot and re-evaluate its marginal contribution.

children.name: Prune or restore members by ablation
children.description: Compare leave-one-out, single-member, and restored-member predictions to retain a compact subset that improves the ensemble.

children.name: Change stacker input features
children.description: Add or remove aligned out-of-fold predictions, embeddings, or auxiliary features and validate their marginal value to the meta-learner.

children.name: Change the combination rule
children.decision: Which rule should combine the available prediction sources?
children.description: Choose a blending rule according to calibration, validation support, and target metric.

children.name: Use equal averaging
children.description: Compare a normalized uniform average with tuned or more complex combinations when reliable evidence for unequal weighting is weak.

children.name: Tune positive blend weights
children.description: Search coarse-to-fine nonnegative weights on aligned validation predictions and re-tune after member or preprocessing changes.

children.name: Give a weak auxiliary model little weight
children.description: Probe small positive weights for an auxiliary source while retaining the strong baseline and measuring incremental value.

children.name: Test signed blend weights
children.description: Compare a constrained negative auxiliary weight with zero and positive weights when residual correction may require subtraction.

children.name: Fit an out-of-fold meta-learner
children.description: Fit and validate a regularized meta-learner on aligned out-of-fold base predictions and compare it with simple blending.

children.name: Change meta-learner complexity
children.description: Compare meta-learner families, penalties, or search ranges while holding the out-of-fold input matrix fixed.

children.name: Normalize ranks before blending
children.description: Compare raw-score blending with rank-normalized or robustly normalized member predictions when output scales differ.

children.name: Choose probability or logit blending
children.description: Compare averaging probabilities with combining logits followed by the appropriate link, checking valid final distributions.

children.name: Change repeated-model aggregation
children.decision: Which repeated prediction source should be added or selected?
children.description: Choose folds, independent training seeds, or inference-time views according to the observed variability.

children.name: Select and average fold checkpoints
children.description: Compare the number or subset of compatible fold models and combine their predictions with normalized averaging.

children.name: Weight fold predictions by evidence
children.description: Compare uniform fold averaging with fold-specific weights supported by validation quality.

children.name: Average independent training runs
children.description: Compare increasing or pruning independent seeded model runs while keeping architecture and data policy fixed.

children.name: Average valid input views
children.description: Compare multi-crop, geometric, temporal, or domain-symmetry test-time views with unchanged inference and verify target invariance.

children.name: Average stochastic forward passes
children.description: Explicitly enable stochastic inference where intended and compare repeated-pass averaging with deterministic evaluation.

children.name: Average compatible model weights
children.description: Average weights from compatible checkpoints of one model and validate the resulting model against prediction averaging.

children.name: Use deterministic evaluation mode
children.description: Disable unintended dropout or dynamic stochastic inference and verify repeated forward passes produce stable predictions.

children.name: Change prediction decoding or calibration
children.decision: Which output adjustment addresses the metric mismatch?
children.description: Choose a post-processing intervention supported by held-out prediction distributions and target semantics.

children.name: Decode predictions onto an ordered label scale
children.decision: Which discretization rule should map scores to allowed labels?
children.description: Choose a global, learned, distributional, or subgroup-specific mapping from continuous predictions.

children.name: Use simple fixed rounding
children.description: Compare clipping and fixed ordinal boundaries with more elaborate calibration and retain the simpler supported mapping.

children.name: Tune global thresholds
children.description: Optimize ordered cutpoints on held-out or out-of-fold predictions and revalidate them when the underlying model changes.

children.name: Match a justified label distribution
children.description: Compare quantile or frequency-based mapping with threshold decoding when the evaluation population’s label distribution is supported by evidence.

children.name: Use subgroup-specific thresholds
children.description: Fit and validate group-specific cutpoints only where groups have adequate representative calibration data.

children.name: Handle discrete ties and degenerate outputs
children.description: Validate per-target discretization, tie handling, and constant-output fallback so rank metrics remain meaningful.

children.name: Restore global thresholds
children.description: Replace unstable or unsupported subgroup-specific cutpoints with one globally validated threshold mapping.

children.name: Calibrate continuous or probability outputs
children.decision: Which systematic prediction defect should be corrected?
children.description: Choose a supported adjustment to location, class balance, or conditional residual error.

children.name: Correct prediction bias or scale
children.description: Fit a held-out offset, scale, or distribution alignment and verify that it changes the task metric rather than merely rescaling ranks.

children.name: Calibrate class distributions
children.description: Compare per-class scaling or probability calibration followed by normalization using held-out class-distribution evidence.

children.name: Apply an auxiliary residual correction
children.description: Tune a small correction from a validated auxiliary head or model while checking output direction and metric effects.

children.name: Apply a validated conditional rule
children.description: Compare a metadata- or subgroup-conditioned output adjustment against the unmodified model using representative held-out examples.

children.name: Keep unmodified continuous scores
children.description: Remove unsupported noise, clipping, or rank-preserving rescaling and compare the original continuous predictions under the actual metric.

unassigned.reason: Only preserves the old parameter block in comments; it proposes no change to modeling, evaluation, or prediction behavior.
Only removes diagnostic displays after correctness is established; no performance or validity change is specified.
Only changes notebook progress-bar display; it provides no modeling, evaluation, or prediction-validity intervention.
